captions: Let's break down the Optimystix Entertainment I-P-O —
a hundred and eight crore S-M-E issue from the production house behind shows like Comedy Circus and Crime Patrol.
We'll cover what it does, its financials,
where the money goes, and what it takes to apply.
This is education, not investment advice.
So what does Optimystix do?
It's a television and content production house —
the team behind well-known shows like Comedy Circus and Crime Patrol.
It has a deep library: over a hundred and fifty T-V shows and more than seven thousand five hundred hours of original programming,
across television and films.
It's led by industry veterans Vipul D.
Shah and Rajesh Bahl,
and this is its first-ever public issue.
Now the financials.
Revenue was fairly steady — up about nine percent,
from a hundred and twenty-five point zero seven crore to a hundred and thirty-five point eight nine crore.
But profit grew much faster — up thirty-nine percent,
from seventeen point two four crore to twenty-four point zero four crore.
So margins improved sharply.
On our estimate,
from a post-issue value of about four hundred and five crore,
that's roughly seventeen times earnings —
a reasonable valuation for a profitable content business.
Where does your money go?
Of the roughly one hundred and eight crore issue,
about eighty-seven crore — some eighty-one percent —
is a fresh issue going into the company.
The remaining twenty-one crore is an offer for sale,
where promoter Vipul D.
Shah sells part of his stake.
So this is a mostly-fresh issue —
four-fifths funds the business.
A healthy structure.
What does the fresh money fund?
The bulk — about fifty-five point eight eight crore —
goes into working capital.
That makes sense for a content producer: you pay crews,
cast and production costs upfront,
and only collect revenue later,
so growth ties up a lot of cash.
The rest is for general corporate purposes.
It's a straightforward, growth-oriented use of the money.
Should you subscribe?
The strengths — it's genuinely profitable,
with recognisable titles and a sharp jump in margins; about eighty-one percent of the issue is fresh money; and at roughly seventeen times earnings,
the valuation is reasonable.
The watch-outs — content is a hit-driven business,
so revenue can be lumpy year to year; top-line growth here was modest,
under ten percent; and it's a small S-M-E,
so volatile and thinly traded.
The takeaway — a profitable,
well-known content house at a fair price, but a hit-driven,
small-cap bet.
Decide with that in mind.
Now — how to apply.
Optimystix lists on the N-S-E S-M-E platform,
separate from the mainboard.
As with all S-M-Es, the minimum is large —
around one lakh rupees or more for a single lot,
far above a mainboard I-P-O.
The exact lot size is confirmed just before the issue opens,
so check it on the day.
And remember, S-M-E stocks are volatile and thinly traded,
so invest only what you can afford to lock away.
Track the live subscription and the final lot on the N-S-E S-M-E page,
Chittorgarh, or your broker app —
allotment is by lottery if oversubscribed.
Let's recap Optimystix Entertainment.
The production house behind Comedy Circus and Crime Patrol,
with a deep library and a sharp jump in margins —
profit up thirty-nine percent.
The issue is about eighty-one percent fresh,
mainly funding working capital,
at a reasonable seventeen times earnings.
But content is hit-driven and lumpy, it's a small S-M-E,
and the minimum bid is around one lakh rupees or more.
This video explains the IPO for education only —
it is not investment advice,
not a buy or sell recommendation,
and not a prediction of listing gains.
Grey-market premium is unofficial and changes hourly.
Always read the RHP and check the live subscription before you apply.
Thanks for watching.
